previous_round.lesson: round 1 left neither stage nor reason; round 2 must (a) prove the OSS gap by evidence instead of assuming it blocks the work, (b) anchor on literature/analytic references when no OSS twin exists, (c) emit machine-checkable numbers before any narrative.

kind: cross-validation (XVAL) of the LBM/DEM coupling stack when the OSS inventory holds NO DEM/granular twin

decision.question: The OSS cache holds three LBM/SPH repositories and zero DEM/granular-contact repositories, so the DEM leg of TensorLBM cannot be cross-validated against an OSS twin. Can it instead be validated to <15% against closed-form / literature references, and what is the state of the fluid-side (LBM) leg that such a coupling would consume?
alternatives: H1: every DEM-side arm (contact restitution, contact duration, peak overlap, terminal settling under the Stokes and Schiller-Naumann closures, momentum-exchange ledger) reproduces its closed-form / literature reference to <15% => the DEM leg is VALIDATED against method-lineage anchors and the missing OSS twin is not a blocker.
H2: some DEM-side arm exceeds 15% => record which one, why (model clipping / integrator order / closure mismatch), and mark that sub-capability WITHHELD in this round.

H3: the closed-form reference itself is reproduced only because the arm is a tautology (the solver and the reference share the same formula) => declare the arm non-evidential and remove it from the acceptance set. This applies to the drag-closure settling arm: it checks the force->acceleration->velocity plumbing, NOT the closure physics, so the acceptance verdict is carried by the literature-anchored arm(s).

H4-falsification: if the fluid-side drag measured by this repo's LBM differs from the literature Cd(Re) curve by >15% at the same Re, then the LBM leg is NOT admissible as a reference for the DEM force model, and this must be reported as a finding rather than hidden by choosing a favourable band.
decision.rule: An arm passes iff |sim - reference| / |reference| < 0.15 (owner precision standard) at the finest resolved time step. The overall anchor passes iff at least one non-tautological DEM arm passes AND no passing arm was obtained at a resolution flagged as unconverged. The LBM leg is reported with the same 15% rule but does not gate the DEM verdict.

hypotheses.contact: Kelvin-Voigt normal contact in this repo (f_n = k*delta - eta*v_n, no tension) integrated by explicit Euler reproduces e = exp(-pi*zeta/sqrt(1-zeta^2)) and t_c = pi/(omega_n sqrt(1-zeta^2)) for zeta = eta/(2 sqrt(k m)), within a few percent, and monotonically improves as dt/t_c shrinks. Prediction: e_sim >= e_th (the no-tension clip removes damping in the restitution phase).
hypotheses.settling: With buoyancy folded into g_eff = g(1-rho_f/rho_p), the DEM ODE with the repo drag closures must converge to the same terminal velocity that drag_closure.terminal_velocity() solves for the same closure (this is a plumbing check, H3 tautology), and the Schiller-Naumann arm must land on the literature (Clift-Gauvin) terminal velocity curve because SN and CG agree to <1% for Re < 40.
hypotheses.ledger: MomentumExchange.residual() must close to round-off (< 1e-10 relative) for a callback-driven drag run, i.e. the particle impulse and the independently recomputed water reaction are the same number.
hypotheses.lbm_leg: The repo's confined periodic-box LBM over-predicts Cd relative to Clift-Gauvin at low Re because lambda = D/L = 1/8..1/6 confinement is only partially removed; prediction: +10..+25% at Re <= 10.

arms.A1: particle-wall restitution vs closed form, dt = t_c/40
arms.A2: particle-wall restitution vs closed form, dt = t_c/80 (resolution-refined)
arms.B1/B2: the same two runs: contact duration t_c and peak overlap delta_max vs closed form
arms.C1/C2: Stokes-closure settling of an ice sphere in water, three diameters, two time steps (tau_p/25, tau_p/100) vs u_t = (rho_p-rho_f) g D^2/(18 mu)  [tautology check H3]
arms.D1/D2: Schiller-Naumann settling vs the literature (Clift-Gauvin) terminal velocity, same three diameters and two time steps
arms.E: repo LBM confined-box Cd(Re) from benchmarks/pending/sphere_drag_closure/results.json vs Clift-Gauvin — the fluid-side leg (not gating)
arms.F: momentum-exchange ledger residual for a cw_callback drag run

secondary: dt-refinement ratio between the two time steps
measured Re for every settling point
max overlap in units of particle radius
metrics.threshold: 0.15 (owner standard); in-house stricter reporting for the closed-form contact arms: 0.02
metrics.unit_of_analysis: one (arm, case, time step) configuration; deterministic, no seeds needed

repetitions.rationale: the quantities are deterministic ODE solutions; the only free numerical parameter is dt/t_c, so two resolutions bound the discretisation error and demonstrate the convergence direction. No stochastic seeds are involved.

external_anchors.restitution: Di Renzo & Di Maio 2004, Chem. Eng. Sci. 59, 525-541 (e vs damping for the linear model); Tsuji et al. 1993, Powder Technol. 71, 239-250
external_anchors.calibration_hierarchy: Coetzee 2017, Powder Technol. 310, 104-113 (analytic -> unit tests -> bulk calibration)
external_anchors.drag_closure: Schiller & Naumann 1935, VDI Z. 77, 318-320; Clift, Grace & Weber 1978, Bubbles, Drops and Particles
external_anchors.settling_benchmark: ten Cate et al. 2002, Phys. Fluids 14, 4012-4024 (single sphere settling, the standard LBM/DEM validation case)
external_anchors.lb_coupling: Tsuji et al. 1993; Ladd 1994, J. Fluid Mech. 271, 285-309 (momentum exchange)
external_anchors.confinement: Hasimoto 1959, J. Fluid Mech. 5, 317-328 (periodic-array drag correction)
